l Heritage Council Act No. 11 of 1999 and operates under the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture (DSAC). The NHC is mandated to preserve, protect, promote, and coordinate heritage in South Africa. The NHC continues to experience increasing demand for: • Heritage conservation support; • Community heritage initiatives; • Research and digitisation; • Indigenous Knowledge Systems preservation; • Public education and awareness; • Heritage partnerships and stakeholder engagement. Despite increasing demand, the organisation remains largely dependent on annual transfers from National Treasury through DSAC. Ongoing fiscal constraints and budget reductions have significantly affected the NHC’s ability to fully implement strategic progr ammes and support the broader heritage sector. This funding gap highlights the urgent need for: • Diversified revenue streams; • Innovative funding mechanisms; • Strategic partnerships; • Heritage commercialisation opportunities; and • Sustainable resource mobilisation interventions. The NHC therefore seeks to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced professional service provider to develop a comprehensive Funding, Resource Mobilisation and Revenue Enhancement Strategy for the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) period 2026/27 – 2

OVERVIEW As part of Cape Town’s Waste Strategy, the City , through the Urban Waste Management (UWM) Directorate, aims to progressively increase access to recycling services to additional households in Cape Town, including low income households. Research has confirmed that residents living in low -income areas often prefer to receive an incentive such as money or goods in exchange for their recyclables. The mobile Swop Shop model, where residents can exchange their packaging waste for grocery items or secondhand items, has been shown to be a successful and cost effective model to deliver a waste minimization service in low income areas. As such, the City has successfully trialed a custom Swop Shop trailer, both in 2020, where 98.7 tons was diverted in 5 months, and in 2022/23, enabling the diversion of 82.7 tons in 12 months. The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions.
